description: Feed-through marshalling for two sensors, operator station requests, a PLC-driven field indicator, and separate protective-earth boundaries.

sheets.name: XT6 field indicator from DQ a.0

properties.signalConfigurationNote: Illustrative connection assumes OUT2 configured for 0–10 V.

objects.text: XT1 · CONTROLLER MARSHALLING
XT0 is the external supply boundary. A1 sensor supply feeds XT1; X10:7 receives the PNP switching signal.
Reference drawing. External supply hardware, cable construction, conductor sizing and PLC logic remain unassigned.
XT2 · FIELD SENSOR MARSHALLING
W-01 cores 1, 2 and 3 carry sensor supply, return and switching signal through XT2.
Reference drawing. External supply hardware, cable construction, conductor sizing and PLC logic remain unassigned.
XT3 · OPERATOR STATION MARSHALLING
W-02 carries a common feed, a normally open Start request and a normally closed operational Stop request.
Reference drawing. External supply hardware, cable construction, conductor sizing and PLC logic remain unassigned.
XT4 · PROTECTIVE-EARTH DISTRIBUTION
Incoming PE is routed separately to the field equipment and operator enclosure terminal boundaries.
Reference drawing. External supply hardware, cable construction, conductor sizing and PLC logic remain unassigned.
XT5 · FIELD PRESSURE INPUT
W-03 carries external +24 V, the shared 0 V reference and B2 OUT2 to A1 AI0.
Reference drawing. External supply hardware, cable construction, conductor sizing and PLC logic remain unassigned.
XT6 · PLC FIELD INDICATION
W-04 carries DQ a.0 switched power and 0 V to the H1 indicator.
Reference drawing. External supply hardware, cable construction, conductor sizing and PLC logic remain unassigned.
The Stop contact documents a PLC input request. Emergency-stop and safety functions are outside this drawing.
The drawing defines terminal connectivity. Physical bonding paths, rail mounting and protective-conductor sizing require review.
Set OUT2 to voltage mode and verify load and scaling against actual equipment. OUT1 is unused; no process range is assigned.
H1 indicates an energized output. The drawing leaves its PLC command and process meaning unassigned.
